bug_description.normalized: The saved 160-byte witness reaches OpenThread's `/c/es` energy-scan request parser and supplies Channel Mask TLV bytes `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00`. `ChannelMaskTlv::GetChannelMask(aMessage)` copies that 8-byte TLV into stack local `channelMaskTlv`; the TLV header says `Length = 6`, while the first entry says `MaskLength = 3`, so `GetFirstEntry()` accepts a 5-byte first entry and leaves one trailing byte inside the TLV. `ChannelMaskEntryBase::GetNext()` therefore returns a non-null second-entry pointer to that final trailing byte, and vulnerable `ChannelMaskTlv::GetChannelMask()` lacks the later fix's full-entry bound check before reusing that pointer as a `ChannelMaskEntry`. On the witnessed run the trailing byte is `0x00`, so the 2.4GHz branch calls `ChannelMaskEntry::GetMask()`, which reads 4 bytes past the 8-byte stack object and triggers the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the malformed Channel Mask TLV on the crashing path. This statement copies the witness's exact bytes `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00` into stack local `channelMaskTlv`.
source.value_from: The staged 160-byte `poc` is consumed by `tests/fuzz/ip6_send.cpp`: byte 0 only sets `settings.mLinkSecurityEnabled`, and bytes 1..159 are appended as a raw IPv6 packet. After IPv6, UDP, CoAP, and `/c/es` resource dispatch, the payload still contains valid Count (`36 01 1f`), Period (`37 02 01 00`), and ScanDuration (`38 02 00 00`) TLVs plus the malformed Channel Mask TLV `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00`, which line 257 copies into `channelMaskTlv`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This copy materializes the attacker-controlled TLV header and first entry bytes that drive the overflow: `channelMaskTlv.GetLength()` becomes `6`, and the first entry's `MaskLength` byte is `3`.

root_cause.description: The loop reuses any non-null pointer returned by `GetNext(this)` as a full `ChannelMaskEntry` without checking that `entry + 1` still fits inside the TLV. The fix adds exactly `VerifyOrExit((cur + 1) <= end && cur->GetNext() <= end);` before any dereference.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The bogus second-entry pointer starts at `channelMaskTlv + 7`, so its `mMask` field begins at `channelMaskTlv + 9`, one byte past the 8-byte stack object `channelMaskTlv` identified by ASan as `[32,40)` in the crashing frame.

parser_admitted.description: CoAP option parsing has already matched the request URI to `/c/es`, so the energy-scan resource handler runs. Inside `EnergyScanServer::HandleRequest`, the POST-code check and the Count/Period/ScanDuration TLV lookups all succeed before execution reaches the Channel Mask lookup at `meshcop_tlvs.cpp:257`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness takes the staged 160-byte witness, uses byte 0 only for `mLinkSecurityEnabled`, appends bytes 1..159 as a raw IPv6 packet, and calls `otIp6Send`.

After IPv6, UDP, and CoAP routing, the `/c/es` resource handler accepts the request as a POST and validates the Count, Period, and ScanDuration TLVs, then asks `ChannelMaskTlv::GetChannelMask(aMessage)` to parse the Channel Mask TLV.
The parser copies the exact 8-byte Channel Mask TLV `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00` into stack local `channelMaskTlv`.

The first entry is admitted using the attacker-controlled `MaskLength = 3`, so `GetNext()` computes a 5-byte step and returns a non-null second-entry pointer to the TLV's final trailing byte. The vulnerable loop lacks the patch's full-entry bounds check before dereferencing that pointer as a `ChannelMaskEntry`.

On the witnessed run the trailing byte equals `0x00`, so the 2.4GHz branch reaches `GetMask()` and reads 4 bytes past the 8-byte stack object `channelMaskTlv`, matching the ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. This copies the exact malformed TLV bytes `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00` into stack local `channelMaskTlv`. The copied object therefore has `Length = 6`, first-entry `ChannelPage = 0xf8`, first-entry `MaskLength = 3`, and a final trailing `0x00` byte at offset 7.

The first-entry admission check passes because the attacker-controlled TLV length is `6` and the first entry's computed size is only `5` (`sizeof(ChannelMaskEntryBase) + MaskLength = 2 + 3`). No `ChannelMaskEntry::IsValid()` or fixed-size `ChannelMaskEntry` check rejects this truncated first entry.

Using the accepted first entry's `MaskLength = 3`, `GetEntrySize()` becomes `5`, so `GetNext()` computes the next-entry start as five bytes after the first entry. Relative to the start of `channelMaskTlv`, that lands at offset 7: the TLV's final trailing byte.

The TLV end is `GetValue() + GetLength()`, which is `channelMaskTlv + 8`. Because the computed next-entry pointer is `channelMaskTlv + 7`, the predicate `entry < end` is true, so `GetNext()` returns a non-null second-entry pointer that actually aliases only the final byte of the TLV.

Root cause. The loop only checks that `entry` is non-null before treating it as a full `ChannelMaskEntry`. It never enforces the later patch's per-iteration bound check `VerifyOrExit((cur + 1) <= end && cur->GetNext() <= end);`, so the non-null pointer to `channelMaskTlv + 7` survives into the next dereference.

On the second iteration, `entry` points at `channelMaskTlv + 7`, so `GetChannelPage()` reads the TLV's final trailing byte. In the saved witness that byte is `0x00`, so the 2.4GHz branch is taken. The crash stack at line 242 shows this branch reached the subsequent mask read.

ASan sink. The bogus second entry starts at `channelMaskTlv + 7`; within a `ChannelMaskEntry`, `mMask` begins two bytes later, so this inline helper performs a 4-byte read starting at `channelMaskTlv + 9`, one byte past the 8-byte stack object. ASan reports the read at stack offset 41 over `channelMaskTlv` `[32,40)` in the frame for `meshcop_tlvs.cpp:255`.

crash_stack.function: ot::Ip6::Ip6::HandleDatagram(ot::Message&, ot::Ip6::Netif*, signed char, void const*, bool)

format.name: OpenThread ip6-send raw IPv6 witness
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 160 bytes. Byte 0 is only used by the harness for `settings.mLinkSecurityEnabled` (`0x6d & 1 == 1` in the saved file); bytes 1..159 are appended unchanged as a raw IPv6 packet. That packet must route to the CoAP `/c/es` energy-scan resource and contain valid MeshCoP Count (`36 01 1f`), Period (`37 02 01 00`), and ScanDuration (`38 02 00 00`) TLVs plus the exact malformed Channel Mask TLV bytes `35 06 f8 03 00 00 00 00`, so the copied stack `channelMaskTlv` has `Length = 6`, first-entry `MaskLength = 3`, and a final trailing zero byte that becomes the bogus second entry's `ChannelPage` on the witnessed run.
